title: Operator steering canvas and SLO restoration guide
author: Elena Morales
content:
Overview:

This page documents the Operator Steering Canvas (OSC) — a compact, action-first framework for incident orchestration focused on restoring SLOs quickly while preserving evidence for postmortem and customer communications. The OSC complements existing runbooks by providing a single source-of-truth during fast-moving on-call events: who is steering, what decisions are permissible, and which artifacts must be captured.

Objectives:
- Restore customer-facing SLOs (latency, availability, correctness) within defined timeboxes.
- Produce a clear, audit-ready evidence trail for postmortem and compliance.
- Minimize blast radius via safe, reversible actions.
- Provide standard, templated status messages for customer and internal comms.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all Redwood-hosted inference endpoints and Dedicated clusters.
- Not intended for long-term reliability projects (use stability initiatives).
- Use OSC for Severity 1/2 incidents and any multi-region degradation that affects >=5% of requests.

Role matrix (who does what):
- Incident Steward (primary): leads the OSC, coordinates contributors, makes go/no-go decisions for fallbacks and rollbacks.
- Bridge Operator (secondary): runs the operational bridge, ensures status cadence and message publication.
- SRE Triage: collects telemetry and executes low-risk mitigations (restart pods, evict noisy tenants).
- Model Steward (ML Eng): responsible for model-related rollbacks, quality checks, and verification prompts.
- Customer Liaison (CS): prepares customer-facing messages and runs customer lane communications.
- Evidence Officer: tags logs/traces, preserves traces, and ensures replay artifacts capture.

Incident lifecycle: concise steps (OSC-driven):
1. Detect & Acknowledge (0-2 min)
   - Alerting: Pager triggers to Incident Steward and Bridge Operator.
   - Quickly validate signal: check metrics dashboard (SLO panel) and alerting fingerprints.
2. Stabilize (2-20 min) — prioritize SLO restoration over root cause
   - Triage owners execute quick mitigations from the Escalation Chord (see table below).
   - If mitigation restores SLO within T1 (20m), proceed to Contain & Monitor.
3. Contain & Communicate (20-60 min)
   - Publish initial status: severity, impact, ETA for next update, affected regions/tenants.
   - Start evidence collection: save spans, snapshot CVM logs, persist current KV-cache state if feasible.
4. Remediate or Fallback (20-180 min)
   - Apply fallbacks in order: routing to cheaper model variant, circuit breaker adjustments, capacity burst.
   - If remediation requires deploy-level change, use a canary/quick rollback plan with explicit steering approval.
5. Recover & Verify (within SLA window)
   - Confirm SLOs are stable for 15m post-action. Run smoke prompts for model correctness.
6. Close & Postmortem (24–72h)
   - Convert OSC artifacts into a postmortem draft. Owner: Incident Steward. Evidence Officer attaches preserved artifacts.

Escalation Chord (safe-first mitigations):
| Order | Action | Owner | Risk | Reversible? | When to use |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | Route traffic to regional fallback (same model) | Bridge Operator | Low | Yes | Region-level perf blips |
| 2 | Switch to quantized model variant (vX.q8) | Model Steward | Medium | Yes | Token-level CPU/GPU pressure |
| 3 | Enable aggressive batching window for non-interactive routes | SRE Triage | Medium | Yes | Cost/backpressure events |
| 4 | Throttle noisy API keys / tenants | SRE Triage | Medium | Yes | Noisy neighbors causing SLO breaches |
| 5 | Scale Dedicated pool (burst capacity) | Infra Ops | High | Yes (auto) | Sustained throughput spike |
| 6 | Emergency rollback of last deployment | Service Owner | High | Yes | Rolling regressions tied to deploy |

Runbook quick-links and snippets (executable actions):
- Kill and restart model worker: kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/model-worker-{{MODEL_NAME}}
- Evict noisy pod (non-draining): kubectl -n infra delete pod {{POD_ID}} --grace-period=0 --force
- Snapshot Prometheus series: promtool tsdb snapshot --labels='release={{INCIDENT_ID}}'
- Export span set (tempo): tempo-cli export --from={{START}} --to={{END}} --query='service="inference" and traceId={{TRACE}}' > evidence-{{INCIDENT_ID}}.json

Steering rules (decision lattice):
- Rule 1: Prefer reversible, application-level mitigations before infra-scale changes.
- Rule 2: Any action that changes model outputs (switching model variant, rollbacks) requires explicit Incident Steward + Model Steward sign-off.
- Rule 3: Customer-impacting throttles require CS notification before enforcement unless immediate SLO restoration is required.

Status page templates (publish via Status Automation):
- Initial public status (short form):
  Title: [Investigating] Degraded inference latency in US-West ({{INCIDENT_ID}})
  Body: We are investigating increased request latency affecting a subset of inference requests in US-West. Impact: ~{{PCT}} of requests. ETA for next update: {{ETA_MIN}} minutes. No action required from customers at this time.
- Update (containment achieved):
  Title: [Update] Containment achieved — latency reduced ({{INCIDENT_ID}})
  Body: We implemented regional routing and temporary batching for non-interactive routes. Latency is trending back within SLOs. We will continue to monitor and post a follow-up within 60 minutes.
- Resolution:
  Title: [Resolved] US-West latency incident ({{INCIDENT_ID}})
  Body: The latency regression has been resolved. Root cause investigation is in progress and will be published in a postmortem within 72 hours.

Customer comms tonebook (short rules):
- Be clear and factual. Avoid speculation.
- Acknowledge customer impact, actions taken, and next steps.
- Use templated slots: Impact, Scope, Workaround (if any), ETA, Next update, Contact lane.

Example customer email (template):
Subject: Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — Degraded latency in US-West\nHello {{CUSTOMER_NAME}},\nWe detected elevated latency affecting a subset of inference requests for your account beginning at {{START_TIME}} UTC. Our engineering team implemented a regional routing mitigation that reduced latency; we are continuing verification. Impact: intermittent slower responses for up to {{PCT}} of requests. Immediate action required: none. ETA for full restore: {{ETA}}. We will follow up with a timeline for root cause and remediation.\nRegards,\nRedwood Inference Support\n
Game day scenario and scoring (15–90m exercise):
- Objective: validate OSC flow end-to-end using a synthetic token storm + model-quality regression trigger.
- Setup: introduce a controlled 30% increase in short-sequence requests to US-West + inject mild model hallucination on canary.
- Roles: assign Incident Steward, Bridge Operator, Evidence Officer, Model Steward, CS Liaison.
- Exercise timeline: detect -> restore SLO using Escalation Chord -> publish status -> close.
- Scoring: time to containment (30m target), evidence completeness (5 artifacts required), customer message quality (peer review).

Postmortem and action items cadence:
- Draft: Incident Steward drafts within 24h with timeline, decisions, and action owners.
- Review: Cross-functional review within 72h.
- Severity remediation: P0 actions (must-do) assigned with owner and committed ETA.
- Retro: 1-week stabilization follow-up to verify fixes are effective.

SLO restoration ladder (operational thresholds):
| Metric | SLO | Alert threshold | First action |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 95th latency (inference-gen) | <200ms | >220ms for 3m | Route region fallback |
| Error rate (500s) | <0.5% | >1% for 2m | Throttle noisy tenants & collect traces |
| Availability (per-customer) | 99.9% monthly | Drop below 99.7% | Burst Dedicated pool + notify CS |

Evidence checklist (must capture during incident):
- Incident timeline (automated) exported and annotated.
- Traces and spans for impacted windows (Tempo export).
- Log snapshot (CVM + model-worker) with correlated trace IDs.
- Config/snapshot of traffic router (hashes, routing table).
- Model binary/version + quantization flags at time of impact.

Runbook governance and ownership:
- All runbooks referenced by OSC must include: last-tested (date), test-owner, safe-rollback steps, and estimated blast radius.
- Runbook retirement follows a 2-step approval: Service Owner + SRE Guild sign-off.

Appendices:
A. Quick-run checklist for the Bridge Operator (first 12 minutes)
1. Acknowledge incident and create INCIDENT_ID in bridge tool.
2. Publish initial status template (short form).
3. Confirm telemetry snapshots are running (Prometheus/Tempo).
4. Execute first-order mitigations from Escalation Chord.
5. Assign Evidence Officer and confirm artifact collection.

B. Template variables (copyable):
- {{INCIDENT_ID}}, {{START_TIME}}, {{PCT}}, {{ETA}}, {{CUSTOMER_NAME}}, {{MODEL_NAME}}, {{POD_ID}}, {{TRACE}}

C. Sample CLI snippets (safety-first)
- Switch routing weight: curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/v1/routing/weights -d '{"region":"us-west","weight":0.7,"incident":"{{INCIDENT_ID}}"}'
- Pause canary deploy: gh api repos/redwood/inference/actions/runs/{{RUN_ID}}/cancel

D. Training & game-day schedule
- Quarterly OSC tabletop (30m) for all oncall teams.
- Semi-annual live game day (2h) with customer-comm simulation.
- New oncall hire: shadow 3 OSC events before solo rotation.

Related resources and links: see Confluence sidebar for runbook library, SLO dashboards, and status automation repo.

Contact and escalation directory: (primary contact first)
- Incident Steward rotation: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.ai
- Bridge Operator: bridge-ops@redwood.ai
- Model Stewarding: models@redwood.ai
- Customer Liaison: cs-ops@redwood.ai
